title: The nightly backup copies the WhatsApp number-check secret and every PIN fingerprint into a plain store for 7 days
what: The nightly backup copies every table of the gym server as it is. It carefully leaves out the passwords of sign-in accounts, but it does not leave out the server's own secrets: the secret that proves a mobile number was checked by WhatsApp (once that row is set live), every owner and desk PIN fingerprint, and the one-time code and sign-in key fingerprints. The copy sits unencrypted in the HQ Worker's Cloudflare store for 7 days and can be turned into a file on a laptop for a restore. Anyone who gets that copy can make their own 'number checked' proof for any mobile, reset that person's PIN and walk into their gym, and can try all one million PINs offline with no lock.
expected: A backup leaves out, or locks with a separate key, every secret it does not need to bring a gym back: the number-check secret, PIN fingerprints and one-time code fingerprints, the same way it already leaves out account passwords.
who: every gym owner and desk person
how_often: only if the backup store or a restore file is seen by the wrong person
fix_line: Leave the number-check secret and the PIN and code fingerprints out of the nightly copy (or lock the copy with its own key), and test that they are absent

items.reason: All 108 functions of 0034-0062 mapped against the catalog. The underscore helpers, every hq_* call (reset owner sign-in, push sender, backup, MettleUp payments and details), every gate_* (entry machine) call and gym_state/gym_has_feature are service_role only (the advisor lists none of them as runnable by anon or signed-in users, which also covers default PUBLIC rights for these definer functions). The rest (member_*, owner_*, staff_*, friend_invite_preview, phone_code_has_account, staff_reset_pin_with_proof, gym_create_online, owner_gym_state) are definer functions any visitor may call; each works out the gym from the key and scopes every read and write to it (read: send message, plan request decision, trainer view, MettleUp payment, mate profile, entry machines). Owner-only saves use the owner-only check; trainer reads refuse an unticked desk. owner_gym_pack and member_gym_pack are not on the live server (0046 not applied). Entry machine registration trusts the serial alone: existing finding reused.

All 41 tables of this area are live with row rules on and 0 policies, so apps cannot read them directly; every reach is through the key-checked functions. Second-gym test per table: staff PINs 0034 step 7; measurements, diet plans 0035 steps 5, 6, 12; timings 0036 steps 3, 5; member days, board, board meta 0037 member view; challenges and hits 0037 step 8 and 0047 step 8; push tokens and push jobs 0038 (the other gym's phone is left out of the send); mate profiles and workouts 0040 step 6; photos 0043 steps 6, 7; plan requests 0044 step 5; report requests and files 0045 steps 1, 3, 6; phone links 0048 step 2; trainers, trainer members, progress summaries 0050 steps 4, 6, 7; workout of the day 0051 step 6; trainer questions 0053 steps 3, 4. Server-only tables (no per-gym rule, so the check is that apps cannot read them): push notes 0054 step 10; payment details, MettleUp payments, payment ledger 0060 steps 10, 14; phone code settings, used proofs, trial phones 0061 step 10; plan features 0062 step 11. Gaps already filed: busy-machine tables (second gym key made, never used), the Bring a friend owner count and the entry machine owner calls (no test) under FN-L3-panel-screens-1-01; entry machine tables read only while empty under FN-L3-server-hq-gate-workers-04.

Rule applied. Tables with no second-gym test: gym_machine_setup, gym_exercise_starts, gym_machine_guesses, gym_friend_invites and gym_friend_referrals (owner side) and the five entry machine tables. Same root causes as two existing lens 3 findings, so those ids are reused instead of a second finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code, tests and the catalog file were read.

All 29 key pattern hits in these files are the role name service_role in grant lines, not keys. The number-check secret is kept only in a closed table, never in git. But the nightly backup copies that secret and the PIN fingerprints out of the database into a plain store: new finding.

No AI or payment key lives in these files. The one key here is the WhatsApp number-check secret: compared safely and readable by no app, but copied into the nightly backup with no lock (same finding).

PIN guessing: 5 wrong tries lock a PIN, 15 minutes then 1 hour, about 120 guesses a day against 1 million PINs; slow fingerprints; a correct sign-in clears the lock. The phone proof is signed, short-lived and used once. But: a PIN or code sign-in makes a session with no end (existing FN-L3-panel-auth-data-01); Forgot PIN resets every person row with that mobile, including one a stranger listed (existing FN-L3-panel-auth-data-02); and the limit of 5 wrong tries per mobile and address in 15 minutes blocks the real owner too, codes included, when every caller shows the same server address (existing FN-L3-server-panel-worker-01).

No typed text is ever pasted into SQL: the only built statement (backup) quotes the table name safely and is HQ-only. Typed text is length-checked and stored as data. The member's workout report file is rewritten by the admin app before download so a cell like =HYPERLINK(...) opens as text.

Two uploads, both into closed tables through key-checked calls: member photo (JPEG start bytes checked, at most 100,000 bytes, only the key's gym and a live member) and the workout report file (only after the member's yes, at most 3 MB, must start with the app's own header, days parsed, only the member's own request). No fault.

Bring-a-friend links use an 8-letter random code from 32 letters (about a million million choices); the page shows only the gym and the sharer's first name; the form is limited to 5 a day per link and 30 per gym. Gym mate profiles open by a random id and only inside the member's own gym. No guessable link here.
This area is database change files only: no package list, no npm or Gradle dependency. The only add-on used is the database's own pgcrypto.
